# David Hume quote sources

8 passages attributed to David Hume in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Hume.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / David Hume

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

English

Cited here from

A Treatise of Human Nature (I.4.6, I.4.7, II.3.3), the Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (V.1, X), the Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, and The Sceptic (1742).

How to cite it

Section and part — Treatise II.3.3 — or the Enquiry's section number. Distinguish the two works: same subtitle, different books, published nine years apart.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Hume reworked the Treatise's material in the first Enquiry and said in his own advertisement that the later work contained his philosophical sentiments and principles. So treating a Treatise passage and an Enquiry passage as interchangeable statements of his view is not safe — where the two diverge, the Enquiry is the revision.

1 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to David Hume?

Section and part — Treatise II.3.3 — or the Enquiry's section number. Distinguish the two works: same subtitle, different books, published nine years apart. This archive cites David Hume from A Treatise of Human Nature (I.4.6, I.4.7, II.3.3), the Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (V.1, X), the Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, and The Sceptic (1742). Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting David Hume?

Hume reworked the Treatise's material in the first Enquiry and said in his own advertisement that the later work contained his philosophical sentiments and principles. So treating a Treatise passage and an Enquiry passage as interchangeable statements of his view is not safe — where the two diverge, the Enquiry is the revision.

### What language did David Hume write in?

English. For an author writing in English the wording is settled at source, but editions and titles are not — see the citation note above.
